correctness.rationale: Every nonzero line direction w in real ell_p^2 has linear nearest-line projection Π_w(x)=w[J_q(w)·x]/(|w1|^q+|w2|^q), because the minimizing residual must be proportional to the duality map of a perpendicular functional. Its rank-one operator norm is R_p(w) and is >=1 by Π_w w=w. Unique nearest-point projection onto any pointed solid cone with independent rays u,v selects from four linear maps I,0,Π_u,Π_v depending on feasible face. Continuity of strict convex metric projections and subdivision of arbitrary line segments where two candidate linear maps agree yield global Lip<=max(1,R_p(u),R_p(v)). For each boundary ray there exists an input with strict KKT inequality on the other ray and positive active-ray coefficient, so a full neighborhood uses Π_u or Π_v; its rank-one norm gives matching lower bound, while the cone interior gives 1. Equality in Hölder for R_p(w)=1 requires p=2, or w with one coordinate zero or equal coordinate magnitudes. Check both independent rays for exact nonexpansivity classification. Independent deterministic candidate-map numerical experiments for p=1.7 and p=3.4 corroborate the sharp constant; optimization solver inaccuracies were resolved by direct candidate verification, not misreported as counterexamples.

originality.rationale: PASS with bounded risk: the published scaled Lorentz cone theorem computes R_p for the two symmetric rays only, not arbitrary skew wedges, and its n>=3 obstruction is irrelevant. Domokos–Marsh supply metric projection and duality-map machinery without an exact all-wedge Lipschitz constant. Real ell_p has few linear isometries for p!=2, so the symmetric wedge result does not imply all asymmetrical cones via rotation. Other projection studies involve weighted ℓ1 balls or Euclidean metric. Possible unindexed classical planar formula remains.
residual_risks: Potential unpublished/older equivalent planar piecewise-linear projection norm theorem could cover the two-ray maximization.

limitations: Only real 2D ell_p, 1<p<infinity, pointed solid cones generated by two independent rays; not general higher-dimensional cones, endpoints p=1 or infinity, or cones containing lines.
